jobs.prompt:
build(cpp): build and test cpp/gateway natively on macOS (Apple Silicon)

CONTINUATION NOTICE (read before the task): an earlier agent ran this same task for about two hours and was cut off. Its work is already in this branch and is yours to continue, not redo: `cpp/gateway/tools/macos-build.sh`, `cpp/gateway/docs/MACOS.md`, the report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-macos-native-20261117.md` (keep this file name and append to it) and Darwin-guarded source and test changes. State at cut-off, per that report: every production source compiles; the runtime tests pass 36/36 binaries and 456/456 cases; the application suite had run 218 targets (205 passing) when it was interrupted, and the 13 non-passing ones share one runner bug (the native working directory is `/private/tmp/...` while the wrapper spelled it `/tmp/...`); a guarded capture-name correction was awaiting recompilation. Start by reading the report's last sections, rebuild with the existing driver, fix the runner path spelling, then run the WHOLE application suite and work through real failures. Because agents can be cut off without warning: commit after every meaningful step and keep the report's counts current as you go.

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
This branch contains `cpp/gateway/`: a finished module-for-module C++20 port of the repository's first-party TypeScript runtime (`src/`, `serve.ts`, `lib/jev_compaction/`): 325 modules (`cpp/gateway/include/uos/**` + `cpp/gateway/src/**`), a JavaScript-semantics runtime layer `uos::rt` (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`), and about 440 test files (`cpp/gateway/tests/**/*_test.cpp`, each a standalone binary using the tiny harness `include/uos/rt/test.hpp`). The TypeScript is the behavioural ORACLE: the port reproduces its behaviour including quirks; expected values in tests were recorded from Bun 1.4.0. The port was written and tested on one Linux/AArch64 host with GCC 12.2 at -O0; other compilers, platforms and sanitizers are being brought up now by agents like you, each on its own clone with its own non-overlapping ownership.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/PORT-NOTES.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/TESTING.md`, `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, and the two reports of agents who already did this kind of bring-up on a runner like yours: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-asan-rt-20261117.md` (ASan/UBSan over the runtime tests with Clang: dependency preparation, flags, a working isolated runner script `cpp/gateway/tests/rt/run_checks.py` you can model yours on) and `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-libcxx-portability-20261117.md` (Clang + libc++ compile of the whole tree). Notes:
- PORTING.md's "Host safety" section and the rule "compile only through tools/unit.sh" exist because the authors' machine is a production server. They do NOT apply on your disposable runner: use compilers directly, build in parallel, use sanitizers and extra build directories freely. All other porting rules (fidelity to the TypeScript, naming, no stubs, the coroutine rules) apply.
- `cpp/gateway/tools/unit.sh`, `tools/env.sh`, `tools/build.py` and the CMake presets are tied to host-specific absolute paths; do not depend on them as they are. Each test's exact source list is in its leading `// Links:` comment or in `cpp/gateway/tests/LINKS.txt`; `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py <test file>` prints the resolved list. Every `src/rt/*.cpp` links into every test binary. Build all sources ONCE into objects or a static library and link each test against it, rather than recompiling per test.
- Port flags: `-std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Wconversion -Werror -DBOOST_JSON_NO_LIB -DBOOST_CONTAINER_NO_LIB -DBOOST_SYSTEM_NO_LIB -I cpp/gateway/include -I cpp/gateway`, linking Boost.JSON, Boost.Container, OpenSSL, pthread, and (dlopen or direct, follow the sources) sqlite3, zlib, brotli, zstd, ICU.

YOUR MACHINE: a fresh GitHub-hosted runner with sudo (where applicable) and network access. Install what you need (recent Clang and/or GCC >= 13: GCC 12 has a coroutine miscompile; CMake, Ninja; OpenSSL, SQLite >= 3.40, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development files; Boost >= 1.83 with Boost.JSON). Bun 1.4.0 is the pinned JavaScript runtime for oracle checks (`bun install --frozen-lockfile` is allowed); when you need to know what the TypeScript does, run it under bun rather than guessing.

RULES
- Fix root causes. Never weaken, skip or delete a test or an expected value; expected values come from Bun. If you believe an expectation is wrong, prove it by running the TypeScript under bun and say so.
- Stay inside the OWNED paths listed below. A defect outside them is REPORTED, not fixed: record it in your findings file with the failing command, the first error lines and your diagnosis. Other agents own the rest of the tree right now and your branch will be merged with theirs: keep every change minimal and local; do not move code, rename things or reformat.
- Do not edit anything under `.github/`, the TypeScript (`src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`), or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`.
- The runner's environment contains a model gateway token: never print it, never write it or any credential into a file. Tests must run with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR`, and provider/credential variables unset.
- Your work is pushed when you stop, even on timeout: keep the tree committable, write your findings file EARLY and update it as you go, and leave no build directories, binaries, large corpora or downloads inside the checkout (build under a temp directory).

FINAL MESSAGE (also the end of your findings file): what you built and how (exact commands), real pass/fail counts, every source change with reason and evidence, what you could not finish, and defects found outside your owned paths.

OWNED PATHS (you may create or edit only these)
- Any file under `cpp/gateway/include`, `cpp/gateway/src`, `cpp/gateway/tests` for DARWIN PORTABILITY ONLY: changes must be inside `#if defined(__APPLE__)` (or equivalent platform) branches or be include/standard-library fixes that cannot change Linux behaviour. Test expectations may gain platform-conditional values proven with Bun on this Mac.
- `cpp/gateway/docs/MACOS.md`, `cpp/gateway/tools/macos-build.sh`
- `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-macos-native-20261117.md`

TASK
You are on a real macOS Apple Silicon runner (Homebrew available, no `apt`). The gateway's second deployment target is the owner's Mac, and it has never been built on one. A previous agent made every translation unit compile with Clang + libc++ on LINUX and added guarded Darwin branches it could not run; read its report (`docs/findings/cppgw-libcxx-portability-20261117.md`) and `cpp/gateway/docs/MACOS.md` first: MACOS.md lists what is unverified. Your job is to verify and finish it on the real thing.
1. Install prerequisites with Homebrew (a recent LLVM if Apple Clang lacks something the tree needs, otherwise prefer Apple Clang; boost, openssl@3, sqlite, icu4c, brotli, zstd, cmake, ninja; bun 1.4.0 for oracle checks) and build ALL of `cpp/gateway/src` into a static library with the port flags. Fix what breaks, inside guarded platform branches (`#if defined(__APPLE__)`), keeping Linux behaviour byte-identical.
2. Build and run all of `cpp/gateway/tests/rt/` first, then as much of the top-level `cpp/gateway/tests/` as possible. For every failure decide, with evidence, whether it is (a) a Darwin portability defect in the port (fix it), (b) a test expectation that encodes Linux facts where the TypeScript would behave differently on macOS: run the same TypeScript under bun ON THIS MAC to see what Bun returns on Darwin (errno values and messages, `process.platform`/`arch`, `os.tmpdir()`, path separators and `/private/var` realpaths, `O_*` constants, signal numbers, unix-socket path limits, `fs.constants`, error texts from `dlopen`, DNS and TLS error texts) and make the expectation platform-conditional with the Bun-on-Darwin value, never by weakening it; or (c) a feature that is Linux-only by design in the TypeScript too (the Landlock/seccomp confinement in `src/runtime/permissions_linux.cpp`: read `src/runtime/permissions-linux.ts` and its callers and mirror what the TypeScript does on darwin).
3. Pay particular attention to: the child-process code (`src/rt/process_loop.cpp`: the Darwin branch uses a SIGCHLD-driven wait instead of pidfd; verify exit codes, kill, stdio piping and no zombie children), the event loop's signal handling, kqueue-backed Asio behaviour differences (half-closed sockets, EPIPE/SIGPIPE: there is no `MSG_NOSIGNAL` on Darwin, check `SO_NOSIGPIPE` is set where the Linux code relies on `MSG_NOSIGNAL`), the dlopen library names (`libz.1.dylib`, `libsqlite3.dylib`, brotli, zstd; prefer Homebrew's SQLite >= 3.40 over the system one if the system one lacks a needed feature, and say which is used), the durable SQLite store (`tests/rt/kv_sqlite_test.cpp`, `tests/kv_durable_*`), the HTTP server and client over loopback and unix sockets, WebSocket tests, TLS certificate verification against the macOS trust store versus the Linux CA bundle, and file timestamps/`utimes` precision.
4. Rewrite `cpp/gateway/docs/MACOS.md` with what is now VERIFIED on macOS (exact macOS, compiler and library versions; exact build and test commands; pass/fail table) and what remains open. Add a script `cpp/gateway/tools/macos-build.sh` that reproduces your build and test run from a clean checkout with no absolute paths of yours.
